sections.what_happened: First Lady Melania Trump will host Russian and Ukrainian representatives at the White House on Thursday Nov 5 at 11:00 ET (20:00 ) and deliver remarks on the Oleshky humanitarian ceasefire (Oct 27-Nov 1), which her office says evacuated nearly 800 civilians. Participants: Ukraine — human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets and MP Davyd Arakhamia; Russia — Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev and human rights commissioner Yana Lantratova (per TASS citing Peskov, 'provided logistical arrangements work out', and Lubinets confirming his travel). New/unresolved details vs the 0900-01 award record: (1) Lantratova is under US sanctions and whether she received authorization to enter the US has not been publicly confirmed (onestnetwork); (2) Kremlin spokesman Peskov told Meduza he knew nothing about the event ('I don't know anything about this. I have no information about it') — directly contradicting the TASS/Peskov confirmation carried by CNA/Kurdistan24; (3) independent verification of the ~800 evacuation total and evacuees' destinations remains limited; (4) the White House has announced no broader negotiating agenda or further evacuation agreement.
sections.what_verified: CNA (T2) + Jerusalem Post (T3) as distinct declared families on the scheduling and participants; Kurdistan24 and Firstpost relay the same announcement (no declared tier — reported with attribution, not counted). The underlying announcement is the White House's own (primary source).
sections.what_disputed: Strongest counterpoint is Peskov's own denial of knowledge of the event (Meduza via dagens) against TASS's Peskov-sourced confirmation — the two cannot both be right about Kremlin awareness. Also: the event is a humanitarian review, not a negotiation — White House framing ('extraordinary moment') vs the limited agenda. Lantratova's sanctions status is an open logistical fact, not yet resolved publicly.
sections.why_matters: Produce AFTER the 20:00 event, not as a preview: lead with the room itself — Russian and Ukrainian officials in the same White House room — then the open questions (did Lantratova get in? did Peskov's denial hold?). The sanctions-entry question is the fault line. Do not present the ~800 evacuation figure as independently verified.
